Resident population of each [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), and [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") in 2024 according to the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau")

The [states and territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States "List of states and territories of the United States") included in the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau")'s statistics for the United States population, ethnicity, and most other categories include the [50 states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") Separate statistics are maintained for the five permanently inhabited [territories of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States"): [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"), the [U.S. Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands"), [American Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa "American Samoa"), and the [Northern Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mariana_Islands "Northern Mariana Islands").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-1)

As of April 1, 2020, the date of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the nine most populous [U.S. states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") contain slightly more than half of the total population. The 25 least populous states contain less than one-sixth of the total population. [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), the most populous state, contains more people than the 21 least populous states combined, and [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming"), the least populous state, has a population less than any of the 31 most populous U.S. cities. The population of Wyoming currently as of 2025 is 588,753.

## Method

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Method")]

The [United States Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census "United States Census") counts the persons residing in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") including [citizens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship "Citizenship"), non-citizen [permanent residents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_residence_(United_States) "Permanent residence (United States)"), and non-citizen long-term visitors.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-2) Civilian and military federal employees serving abroad and their dependents are counted in their home state.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-3)

## Electoral apportionment

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Electoral apportionment")]

Every 10 years, the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau") is charged with making an actual count of all residents by state and territory. The accuracy of this count is then tested after the fact, and sometimes statistically significant undercounts or overcounts occur. For example, for the [2020 decennial census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), 14 states had significant miscounts ranging from 1.5% to 6.6%. While these adjustments may be reflected in government programs over the following decade, the 10-year representative apportionments discussed below are not changed to reflect the miscount.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-4)

### House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: House of Representatives")]

Based on this decennial census, each state is allocated a portion of the 435 fixed seats in the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") (until the early 20th century, the apportionment process generally increased the size of the House based on the results of the census until the size of the House was capped by the [Reapportionment Act of 1929](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reapportionment_Act_of_1929 "Reapportionment Act of 1929")), with each state guaranteed at least one Representative. The [allocation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_congressional_apportionment "United States congressional apportionment") is based on each state's proportion of the combined population of the [fifty states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") (not including the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia "District of Columbia"), [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"), [American Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa "American Samoa"), the [Northern Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mariana_Islands "Northern Mariana Islands"), [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), or the [U.S. Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands")).

### Electoral College

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Electoral College")]

The [Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College"), every four years, elects the [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") and [Vice President of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") based on the popular vote in each state and the District of Columbia. Each state's number of votes in the Electoral College is equal to its number of members in the Senate plus members in the House of Representatives.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5)

The [Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-third_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution") additionally grants the District of Columbia (D.C.), which is not a state, as many Electoral College votes as it would have if it _were_ a state, while having no more votes than the least populous state (Wyoming). Since the U.S. Constitution guarantees every state at least one member of the U.S. House of Representatives and two members of the U.S. Senate, every state has at least three Electoral College votes. Thus, the Electoral College has 538 members (100 [senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"), plus 435 representatives due to the limit imposed by the Reapportionment Act of 1929, plus 3 members for the District of Columbia).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5)[Territories of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States") are not included in the Electoral College: people in those territories cannot vote directly for the President of the United States,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-6) although they may participate in the partisan nominating primaries and caucuses.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-7)

Michigan: Biden 49.5 vs 49.3 diff 0.2%. New Jersey: Biden 57.2 vs 39.0 diff 18%. Virginia: Biden 56.5 vs 38.6 diff 17.9%. Washington: Biden 62.9 vs 28.8 diff 34.1%. Missouri: Trump 53.5 vs 45.6 diff -7.9% <10. Maryland: Biden 61.0 vs 33.6 diff 27.4%. Colorado: Biden 51.6 vs 46.5 diff 5.1% (<10). Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.
